citation: 'Two ice cream concerns to erect plant jointly. Collins Bros. and Thompson-Reid companies buy land and will construct a $40,000 establishment.' Chicago Daily Tribune, 4 September 1903.
author: Chicago Daily Tribune
locator: The real-estate column: '84x170 feet of ground in Indiana avenue, sixty-four feet south of Sixteenth street, west front ... to erect a plant covering the entire property to cost from $35,000 to $40,000. The work of construction will begin in thirty days.' The Sonntagpost of 25 October 1903 names the ground 1605-1613 Indiana Ave., 101 by 170 feet.
rights_note: A US newspaper published in 1903, in the public domain. Read for a sale and a plan.

note: The purchase that ended the two 1886 houses on 1605-1613: bought in September 1903 for a plant to cover the whole ground. The corner lot, the first 64 feet south of 16th Street, was not part of it.
